findings.title: Empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation; a variable that resolves to empty can leave the panel loading forever
findings.body:
`runShardSplitQuery` used to interpolate first (`interpolateVariablesInQueries`) and then drop queries with an empty `expr`. The PR reverses this: `.filter((query) => query.expr)` checks the raw expression and only then calls `applyTemplateVariables`.

A target such as `$query`, where the variable resolves to an empty string, now passes the filter and becomes `expr: ''`. The failure path:
- `requestSupportsSharding([query])` is false for an empty expr, so the query lands in the non-shard `otherQueries` group.
- `runSplitQuery` is called for that group and filters it out, because its `expr` is now empty.
- `runSplitGroupedQueries` receives an empty `requests` array. There `requests.filter(...)[0].partition` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`.
- The throw happens synchronously inside the `groupTargetsByQueryType(...).then(...)` callback. It becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the returned Observable never emits or completes.

Result: any panel mixing a shardable query with a query whose variable resolves to empty hangs in the loading state. Filter on `expr` after interpolating, in both `runShardSplitQuery` and `runSplitQuery`, so empty interpolated queries are dropped. Consider also guarding `runSplitGroupedQueries` against an empty `requests` array.

findings.title: Ad-hoc filters and template variables are applied repeatedly to the same query
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`. The sub-requests it builds keep `request.filters` and are passed to `datasource.runQuery`, which goes through `DataSourceWithBackend.query` and calls `applyTemplateVariables(q, scopedVars, request.filters)` again. On the sharding path it happens a third time: `runShardSplitQuery` also applies the variables and filters, then forwards the request, filters included, into `runSplitQuery`.

Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` adds ad-hoc filters to the expression. Filters added to the stream selector are de-duplicated. For queries with a parser or label filter, though, `addFilterAsLabelFilter` appends a new `| key=`value`` stage on every pass, with no de-duplication. For example, `{app="x"} | json` with ad-hoc filter `level=error` becomes `{app="x"} | json | level=`error` | level=`error`` (three copies on the shard path). The queries sent and shown in the inspector are bloated, and they differ from what the non-split path produces.

Re-running `templateSrv.replace` on already-interpolated text can also re-expand `$name` sequences that came from variable values. The updated shard test expecting `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times encodes this redundant work.

Interpolate once and strip `filters` (or otherwise mark the request as already interpolated) on the sub-requests passed down to `runSplitQuery` and `runQuery`.

findings.title: New interpolation test does not cover the behaviour the fix targets and relies on unrealistic `$__auto` replacement
findings.body:
The test only checks that the targets passed to the mocked `runQuery` are interpolated. In production, `runQuery` (via `DataSourceWithBackend.query`) already interpolated targets before this change. So the assertion does not exercise what the PR actually fixes: `calculateStep`, `isLogsQuery` and `querySupportsSplitting` now see interpolated values, e.g. a `$step` variable changing the step-aligned partition boundaries.

The mock `replace` also rewrites `$__auto` to `5m` unconditionally. The real `applyTemplateVariables` deliberately removes `__auto` from scopedVars so the backend interpolates it, so the test asserts frontend behaviour that never happens. The same pattern is copied into `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`.

Assert on the computed ranges or grouping for an interpolated `step` instead, and use a regular dashboard variable in place of `$__auto`.
